newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Democrats back Labor on pension reforms.
newsitem.headline: Australian Democrats back Labor on pension reforms.

text.p: A key Australian minority party said on Tuesday it would back the Labor opposition's push to exempt some workers from a planned tax surcharge on retirement fund contributions.
Australian Democrats' pension funds spokeswoman Lyn Allison said the party supported Labor's call to protect low paid and sacked workers from the surcharge.

"The Democrats will be supporting two of the key (Labor) ... amendments and they are the ones that seek to protect low income workers and those workers who have lost their jobs and are being retrenched," Allison said.

Labor announced earlier on Tuesday it would oppose the Liberal-National government's plan to impose up to a 15 percent surcharge on retirement fund contributions for workers earning more than A$70,000 a year unless low-paid and sacked workers were spared the extra charge.
That surcharge would be on top of the existing 15 percent tax on contributions to pension, or superannuation, funds.
But Allison stopped short of saying the Democrats would also vote against the legislation imposing the surcharge if the government rejected the Labor amendments.
Labor has warned the reforms would catch up to one million lower income earners who could be pushed above the A$70,000 level by retrenchment payments, insurance payouts or other one-off payments.
The government is in a minority in parliament's upper house, the Senate, and needs the support of at least two non-government senators to pass its legislation.
